introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i)(a) A random variable $X$ has a probability mass function $p(x)$, where

$$
p(x)=\begin{cases}kx^2, & x=1,2,3,4,5\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}
$$

where $k$ is a constant. Copy and complete the table below. *[2 marks]*

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X=x)$ |  |  | $9k$ |  |  |
(i)(b) With $p(x)=kx^2$ for $x=1,2,3,4,5$ (and $0$ otherwise), find the value of $k$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The probabilities must sum to $1$:

$k+4k+9k+16k+25k=55k=1\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{1}{55}.$

**$k=\dfrac1{55}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) Find the mean and the variance of the distribution. *[4 marks]*

(ii) The probability that a watermelon selected at random from a bag is defective is $\dfrac13$. 6 watermelons are selected at random from the bag one after the other without replacement. Using the binomial distribution, find the probability that:

(a) no watermelon is defective. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of defective watermelons among the 6 selected. Using the binomial distribution as the question instructs, $X\sim\text{Bin}\left(6,\dfrac13\right)$ with $p=\dfrac13$, $q=\dfrac23$.

$P(X=0)=\binom60\left(\dfrac13\right)^0\left(\dfrac23\right)^6=\dfrac{64}{729}\approx0.0878.$

**$P(\text{no defective watermelon})=\dfrac{64}{729}\approx0.088$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) With $X\sim\text{Bin}\left(6,\dfrac13\right)$ (6 watermelons, each defective with probability $\dfrac13$), find the probability that less than 2 watermelons are defective. *[3 marks]*
(ii)(c) Find the mean and variance of the distribution $X\sim\text{Bin}\left(6,\dfrac13\right)$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For a binomial distribution $\text{Bin}(n,p)$: mean $=np$ and variance $=npq$.

Mean $=6\times\dfrac13=2.$

Variance $=6\times\dfrac13\times\dfrac23=\dfrac43\approx1.33.$

**Mean $=2$; variance $=\dfrac43\approx1.33$.**
